result: The authors developed a focal laser lesion model using 488 nm light that selectively ablates photoreceptors in the outer nuclear layer with minimal collateral damage to inner retinal structures, vasculature, or the blood-retinal barrier. The lesion produces a hyperreflective phenotype that persists for 7 days and resolves by 2 months, with transient photoreceptor loss (18-27% reduction at 3-7 days) that returns to baseline by 2 months.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly praised this methodological advance. Reviewer 3 stated this is 'one of the major advances in this article' and noted the model uses 'close to 2 orders of magnitude lower laser power than the more prevalent choroidal neovascularization model.' Reviewers affirmed that 'histology and OCT together show that the laser insult is localized to the photoreceptors and spares the inner retina, the vasculature and the pigment epithelium.' No concerns were raised about the characterization of the lesion model.

result: Microglia showed a robust, progressive response to photoreceptor injury, with cells migrating into the outer nuclear layer within 1 day, exhibiting morphological changes from ramified to amoeboid phenotypes, and demonstrating evidence of photoreceptor phagocytosis. By 2 months, microglia returned to their baseline distribution in the inner retina.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly stated 'the time-course, 2D and 3D spatial activation pattern of microglial activation are striking and provide an unprecedented view of the retinal response to mild injury.' Reviewer 2 noted 'an extremely thorough examination of the cellular-level immune activity at the injury site.' The editor affirmed 'the evidence supporting the authors' claims is compelling.' No reviewer challenged the microglial response findings.

result: Despite robust microglial activation and close proximity to retinal vessels carrying neutrophils, neutrophils were not recruited to the injury site at any time point examined (1 day to 2 months). Neutrophils remained within the vasculature and showed no evidence of extravasation, aggregation, or rolling behavior near the lesion.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 identified this as 'one of the main findings of the paper,' stating 'the injury did not seem to result in the extravasation of neutrophils from the capillary network.' Reviewer 2 summarized 'the results suggest that despite the highly active microglia at the injury site, neutrophils were not recruited.' The editor noted the study 'illustrates that microglial activation does not recruit neutrophils.' All reviewers accepted this finding without challenge.

result: The laser lesion did not compromise the blood-retinal barrier or alter retinal vascular perfusion, as demonstrated by lack of fluorescein leakage, maintained blood flow in all vascular layers, and normal capillary flux measurements at lesion sites from hours to months post-injury.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 affirmed that the findings 'show that the laser insult is localized to the photoreceptors and spares the inner retina, the vasculature and the pigment epithelium.' No reviewer questioned the vascular integrity data or raised concerns about the blood-retinal barrier assessment. The claims are treated as established facts supporting the focal nature of the injury model.

result: In the endotoxin-induced uveitis (EIU) positive control model, neutrophils extravasated into the retinal parenchyma and exhibited spherical morphology, contrasting with the pill-shaped morphology of neutrophils confined within capillaries.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 noted 'two different models of inflammation - endotoxin-induced uveitis (EAU) and laser ablation are used to study differences in the immune interaction' as a strength. No reviewer challenged the EIU control data or the morphological distinctions described. The positive control is accepted as validating the ability to detect neutrophil extravasation when it occurs.

result: The laser exposure produced progressive photoreceptor damage with peak cell loss at 3-7 days rather than immediate ablation, suggesting apoptotic or necroptotic death. The hyperreflective phenotype appeared within 30 minutes before microglial aggregation, indicating it is not caused by microglial activity. Photoreceptor nuclear density returned to baseline by 2 months, likely due to adjacent photoreceptors filling the lesion area.
evaluation: These interpretive claims about damage mechanisms and recovery are presented as part of the lesion characterization that reviewers praised. Reviewer 3 stated 'the analysis is sound' and no reviewer challenged these mechanistic interpretations. The temporal sequence data supporting these conclusions (C37, C58) was explicitly accepted as part of the 'striking' time-course analysis.

result: The authors propose that resident microglia may facilitate necessary phagocytic responses without recruiting systemic immune cells, potentially protecting the CNS from propagating larger systemic responses that could exacerbate disease. They suggest damage-associated molecular patterns or chemotactic gradients were insufficient to recruit neutrophils despite strong microglial activation.
evaluation: These speculative mechanistic interpretations are presented in the discussion and were not challenged by any reviewer. The editor stated 'the evidence supporting the authors' claims is compelling' and noted the study 'potentiates future work in the field to better understand the disease process,' implicitly accepting these interpretations as reasonable frameworks for future investigation. No reviewer requested additional experiments to test these hypotheses.

result: The authors propose that AOSLO cellular-level imaging may reveal interactions of multiple immune cell types in the living retina, representing a valuable paradigm for studying immune responses and retinal remodeling in vivo.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly stated 'the demonstrated paradigm of studying the immune response and potentially retinal remodeling in the future in vivo is valuable and would appeal to a broad audience in visual neuroscience.' Reviewer 3 also noted 'adaptive optics imaging of murine retina is cutting edge and enables non-destructive visualization' as a major strength. This forward-looking claim about the technology's potential is affirmed by reviewers.

result: Background claims establishing that microglia and neutrophils are first responders to CNS injury, that their interactions in retinal damage are poorly understood, and describing the immune-privileged status of the retina and normal distribution of microglia.
evaluation: These are standard background claims establishing context for the study. No reviewer challenged any of these foundational statements. They are treated as accepted knowledge that motivates the research questions. Reviewer 2 accurately summarized the study's premise without questioning these background assertions.

result: Methodological details regarding ethical approval, sample sizes (18 mice for in vivo imaging, 10 mice for histology), and age ranges (postnatal weeks 6-24) of experimental subjects.
evaluation: These are standard methodological reporting details that no reviewer questioned or challenged. Reviewer 3 noted 'a few different sets of mouse models are used' as a strength, implicitly accepting the experimental design and sample sizes as appropriate. The editor's note states 'the authors have addressed all the previous concerns raised by the reviewers,' indicating methodological adequacy.
